claims.text: The alloy begins in a single-phase solid-solution state.
Mechanical loading under demanding engineering service conditions causes the alloy to lose toughness.
Mechanical loading under demanding engineering service conditions can cause brittle fracture of the alloy.
The relevant structural mediator is the formation of widely distributed and overlapping energy barriers for multiple plasticity mechanisms.
The distributed energy barriers hinder dislocation motion.
Hindered dislocation motion ultimately produces superplasticity.
Hindered dislocation motion ultimately produces ultrahigh strength.
High temperature and high strain rate are the applicable loading conditions.
The exact temperature and strain-rate ranges for toughness loss or brittle fracture are uncertain.
The hypothesis is falsified if toughness or fracture toughness does not decrease by at least 10% and brittle fracture is not observed under the proposed service conditions.

contradictions.description: The mechanism is said to lead to superplasticity, while the predicted outcome is toughness loss or brittle fracture. Superplastic deformation and brittle fracture are opposing responses unless distinct temperature, strain-rate, size, or microstructural regimes are specified.
